newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul ready for biggest N.Korean defector group.
newsitem.headline: Seoul ready for biggest N.Korean defector group.

text.p: The biggest group of North Korean defectors since the 1950-53 Korean War were heading on Monday to Seoul, where their dramatic escape through China and Hong Kong has raised fears of a mass refugee flight.
The 17 escapees who sneaked into Hong Kong after a month-long trek across China were due to arrive on a scheduled Korean Airlines flight, a foreign ministry spokesman said.
Among them are 16 members of a single family, whose flight was financed by relatives in the United States, and a security guard.
The Korean clan has been joined in Hong Kong by two other North Koreans, at least one an intelligence operative, seeking asylum, Seoul media reported on Sunday.

South Korea once rolled out the red carpet for communist defectors, mostly escaping solo or in groups of twos or threes, but the latest bold escape by a bloc of 17 has raised fears that North Korea may be cracking up.
Recent defectors have been weak and emaciated, reflecting near-famine conditions in much of the North that is struggling to survive the effects of floods and industrial collapse.

An uncontrolled refugee exodus from the North, signalling a breakdown of internal controls -- similar to the German experience -- is part a nightmare scenario for Seoul, which would be left to pick up the pieces from any collapse in Pyongyang.
The North Korean family will be offered asylum and a modest payment by South Korea.
Seoul media have speculated each person will get about 10 million won ($12,000) to help them settle and find work, a sum that will not go far in high-cost South Korea.

The South Korean government is drawing up plans for reception centres for North Koreans -- half-way houses that will offer immediate shelter and vocational training -- and the first could be ready next year.
The 17 arrived in Hong Kong on November 23. They were scheduled to board a flight at 12.50 p.m. Hong Kong time (0450 GMT) and arrive three hours later, the foreign ministry spokesman said.
